facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of diarrhea.
Patient experiences watery loose stools about 5 to 6 times a day.
Symptoms began with vomiting twice and then it resolved.
facts.source_text: began w/ vomiting x2 then resolved

facts.content: There is no blood in the stools.
Patient reports no abdominal pain.
Patient felt feverish early on but now improved.
Patient feels weak and dehydrated.
Patient has poor appetite with minimal solid food intake.
Patient reports no headache or muscle aches.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses a 'blue' inhaler as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer approximately 10 years ago.
facts.source_text: Father HTN; died of bowel ca ~10y ago.

facts.content: Patient's mother has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient lives alone and is a software engineer.
Patient has been off work for the past 3 days.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Patient consumes alcohol infrequently and socially.
Diagnosis of acute gastroenteritis with 3-day watery diarrhea.
Episode of initial vomiting has resolved.
No blood in stools or abdominal pain.
Patient was feverish early but now improved, feeling weak with low oral intake.
facts.source_text: feverish early now improved; weak, low PO

facts.content: No clear exposure leading to symptoms.
Asthma is stable with infrequent use of inhaler.
facts.source_text: 2) Asthma — stable; infrequent use of “blue” inhaler

facts.content: Recommended oral fluids and over-the-counter ORS (Dioralyte) for acute gastroenteritis.
Paracetamol suggested as needed for feverishness and weakness.
Advised to stay off work for 1 to 2 days.
Patient should return to work only after being diarrhea-free for 24 to 48 hours.
Continue using the inhaler as needed for asthma.
Follow up next week if not improved.
facts.source_text: F/U next week if not improved
